scope.purpose: Place related actions together with one size and a consistent spacing, and reflow them when space runs out.
useCases: Dialog footer (Cancel, Save) aligned at the end.
Actions of an Alert or a Toast, of a card or a page header.
A stacked full-width group on a narrow screen (reflow stack).
exclusions: Arrow-key navigation and one tab stop: Toolbar (wave 4).
Attached buttons for a choice: SegmentedControl (later).
Overflow into a More menu: a composition with Menu, not an option.
alternatives: Toolbar for a set of controls acting on one object.
SegmentedControl for a single choice among options.

decisionsTaken: Gap space.control.gap.{size} (6, 8, 10 px, density aware), as the catalog note of 2026-10-20 says.
size is set on the group and applies to every item (the RadioGroup precedent); an item's own size is ignored inside a group.
align start, center, end and stretch for both orientations; no space-between option: a split footer (a destructive action at the start) is two groups in a layout, which keeps reading order explicit.
reflow wrap (default) or stack: stack switches the whole group to vertical full width when it does not fit, observed as the state stacked; the group never reorders items.
No disabled prop: each action is disabled on its own.
label optional: the group is a named group only when it has one.
Stacking is measured, not a container query: a container query would need a threshold width the contract does not have.
Vertical always stretched; no wrap: a line that does not fit stacks (user, 2026-11-03).
nextAction: Wave 4 changes accepted with the wave 4 implementation gate; the Figma master was re-checked at the wave 4 Figma parity (unchanged); the documentation is re-checked with the wave 4 documentation step.
implementationNotes: Button and IconButton read the group size through the context key ggb:button-group (a string; each folder declares the shape again), so an item's own size is ignored inside a group.
A host (Alert) may ask for a default size through the context key ggb:button-group-host; an explicit size on the group wins.

reflow stack: a ResizeObserver compares the extent of the items (first start edge to last end edge, whatever the alignment) with the inline size, stacks the group and remembers that extent to return to the line. In the horizontal layout items never shrink below their content.
Overlays (Popover, Dialog, Menu) clear the ggb:button-group context for their content, so that a group around their declaration does not size their buttons.
